# Detection scoreboard corpus

The frozen, labelled input for `npm run detection:eval` (map #600, ticket #605).
Every Structure Detection change is measured on it, and every engine version
bump attaches its table.

- `labels.json` is hand-edited. A `structured` label takes its rep scheme from
  the athlete's title ("i3 10x3 min, p:60", "20x45/15"), or from a `scheme` the
  athlete confirmed for an untitled session. The rest were labelled by reading
  each run's per-minute power, pace and HR: `unstructured` (steady, long, hilly,
  paused) is scored, and `unlabelled` is reported but never scored.
- `corpus.json` is generated by `npm run detection:corpus` from the owner's FIT
  files (below) and `prisma/seed-data/kody-strava-history.json` and
  `labels.json`. It holds the stream at stored resolution, any stored laps, the
  label and four profiles. The freezer places a title's scheme on the stream by
  fitting its square wave to power, so the work windows are good to about one 5
  s sample.

Read the numbers with these limits in mind:

- **Small and from one athlete.** One positive moves recall by about 9 points.
- **Two profiles leak the labels.** `label-pace` and `label-power` are medians
  of the labelled i3 reps, scored on the same corpus, so they flatter recall and
  robustness. Only `seed` and `hr` are free of that.
- **The truth is a power fit.** Work windows come from fitting the scheme to the
  same power channel the engine reads, so boundary and intensity errors measure
  agreement with that fit. A placement with work/recovery power (`contrast`)
  under 1.5 is the least certain. Checked against the laps of the same 11
  sessions in the FIT half: the fit sits 0–6 s (median) from the lap edges, low
  contrast included. Two Strava labels are wrong in shape: "i3 25x45/15" was 20
  reps, a 7 min break and 5 more, and "i4 13x45/15 motbakke" is 13 only by the
  athlete's word (the laps hold 11 clean reps).

## The FIT half (#625)

The owner's Intervals.icu bulk export (`download-fit-files`, 666 FIT files,
2018–2026, about 55 MB) is the source, used with the owner's consent
(2026-10-20). Files are named `<intervalsIcuId>_<title>.fit`.
`npm run detection:corpus` decodes them
(`app/utils/structure-detection/eval/fit.ts`, on top of the app's `parseFit`),
labels every run or bike session and adds the labelled ones to `corpus.json`
under `fit`, with their laps and label; the stream is decoded from the file at
eval time, so it is not stored twice. Other sports (cross-country ski, strength,
hiking, swimming and the rest) are counted and skipped, as the Strava half skips
them: detection runs for run and bike only.

**The FIT files are never in this repository.** They carry GPS tracks, and this
repository is public. They live in the private
[`leskraas/trainm8-private`](https://github.com/leskraas/trainm8-private) under
`detection/fit/`, and the scripts read them from a clone next to this one
(`../trainm8-private/detection/fit`), or from `DETECTION_FIT_DIR`
(`scripts/detection/fit-dir.ts`). `corpus.json` keeps only each file's name,
laps and label. The private repository holds the files of the structured and
unstructured sessions only; the unlabelled runs and the other sports stay with
the owner, and `corpus.json` keeps only their counts (`fitSummary`). The build
writes a `.gitignore` in the FIT folder to match. To rebuild, copy the full
export into the FIT folder and run `npm run detection:corpus`. Without it, a
labelled session whose file is missing keeps its frozen entry (and the summary
of the build that saw every file), and the eval scores the sessions whose file
is on disk.

- **Labels come from the laps**, not from power: a run of active laps separated
  by rest/recovery laps (a structured workout's steps), or laps that are all
  active but alternate in length or effort (reps lapped by hand); see `lapSets`
  in `eval/label.ts`. Power enters only to tell the work from the recovery in
  hand laps and to drop an easy end lap. The title, and the Strava label of the
  same session, are checked against the laps, and the build prints every
  disagreement.
- Sessions without a lap set take the Strava hand label of the same session
  (matched on start time), else `unstructured` when the planned title is an easy
  run ("Basis", "Restitusjon"), else `unlabelled`.
- `labels.json` → `fit` corrects the few the rules get wrong, each with a note.
- The eval scores them at 1 s (gaps of up to 3 s filled), on the production grid
  (5–6 s), at 15 s, and with the files' laps, for v2 and for the #609 v3
  prototype (`scripts/detection/v3-probe.ts`, eval-only).

What the files are not:

- **Not device originals.** The bulk export returns files Intervals.icu
  generated (as `app/integrations/intervalsicu/types.ts` notes), not the
  originals `GET /activity/{id}/file` returns. Every file's `file_id` says
  `manufacturer = development`, `product_name = Intervals.icu`, with a
  `time_created` of the export, not the activity. The records keep their 1 s
  rate, and the laps keep their edges and an `active`/`recovery` role, but the
  bulk export has no `wkt_step_index`, no `lap_trigger`, no `workout_step`
  program, no `length` messages (the pool swims read `swimming/openWater`), and
  warm-up and cool-down laps are written `active`. The device questions (step
  index reuse, skipped steps, the step program, pool lengths) still need true
  originals.
- **One athlete, mostly one watch.** One positive moves recall by about 1 point;
  the eval prints Wilson intervals beside the main rates.
